Jonas / Laura / Rishi,

Thanks for the ping. I drafted two options — one commercial compromise and one fallback if legal needs firmer guardrails. Key principles: keep title with Redwood, give Cygnus broad product rights, and limit training to opt-in + strict telemetry language.

Option A (preferred compromise — clean):
"Customer Outputs. Redwood hereby grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, transferable license to use, reproduce, distribute, and create derivative products from Outputs generated for Customer under this Order Form. Redwood retains ownership of its models and underlying weights but agrees that it will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to retrain or improve its base models, except as described in the Telemetry and Service Improvement section below."

Telemetry and Service Improvement (attached to be precise):
"Redwood may collect aggregated, anonymized usage metrics and system telemetry for service quality improvements and security; such telemetry shall not contain Customer Content or Outputs in identifiable form and shall not be used to train or fine-tune models that would expose Customer Content."

Option B (if legal requires stronger language):
- Offer a time-limited exclusivity/assignment for Outputs tied to a higher tier purchase, or a fee for assignment.

I've added line edits in the attached RI-proposed-clause.docx so legal can review exact phrasing. My recommendation is to push Option A and offer a one-time fee for assignment only if Cygnus insists.

Attachments:
- RI-proposed-clause.docx (Redwood suggested wording with commentary)

Cheers,

Jonas / Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the draft language. We reviewed Option A internally and legal will accept that approach with one tweak: the clause must guarantee that any telemetry used for service improvements cannot be de-anonymized to reconstruct Customer Outputs, and Cygnus needs a 30-day notice and opt-out window before any change to the feedback/telemetry practice.

Proposed change (in-line):
"Redwood may collect aggregated, anonymized usage metrics and system telemetry for service quality improvements and security; such telemetry shall not contain Customer Content or Outputs in identifiable form and Redwood shall not take any action to de-anonymize telemetry in a manner that could reconstruct Customer Outputs. Redwood shall provide Customer with written notice at least thirty (30) days in advance of any material change to telemetry or feedback practices and Customer may elect to opt out of such practices within such period."

We attached a short response tracker and an updated SLA exceptions sheet for transparency — see response_tracking.pdf and SLA_exceptions.xlsx. Procurement is OK to proceed on principle if you accept the above in the order form.

Thanks — looking to close this by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Best,
